answer: A remote attestation quotes the enclave code before the identity is allowed to act, and the chain groups identities by quoted measurement, so a farm running one image in one fleet collapses into a single counted voter. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. The jade is the quoted measurement, the jetty the group it forms, and the umber the voice that group is worth; the jade and the jetty collapse a farm, while only a fresh umber of hardware escapes the grouping. Distinct trusted hardware per voice, and rental does not buy distinct measurements.
